priya: Heads-up — onboarding a community model hit a weird fast/slow tokenizer split. fast tokenizer missing tokenizer.json, only tokenizer_config.json present, so runtime picked slow path and we lost system special tokens for chat template.
omar: Ugh. Which model and where did the artifacts come from? HF snapshot or converted bundle?
priya: HF snapshot + our converter. bundle has: model.bin, config.json, tokenizer_config.json, merges.txt but no tokenizer.json. fast tokenizer loader expects tokenizer.json to exist.
kevin: Can you paste ls output? quick check:
priya: ```
$ ls -la /mnt/models/xxl-chat/
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000 3.2G Jun 10 model.safetensors
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000  12K Jun 10 config.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000 2.1K Jun 10 tokenizer_config.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000 1.8K Jun 10 merges.txt
-rw-r--r-- 1 1000 1000  10M Jun 10 vocab.json
```
omar: That looks like a fast tokenizer that was partially converted (vocab + merges) but converter didn't emit tokenizer.json. fast->slow fallback will call PreTrainedTokenizerFast.from_pretrained and fail if tokenizer.json missing, else falls back to slow which may not have special tokens metadata.
sophia: I saw this before with quantized bring-ups: when tokenizer.json is absent the KV-cache tokenization offsets differ slightly leading to hallucinated role tokens during chat evals. Might explain the quality regression in the quantization experiment.
kevin: Repro steps: run a short chat prompt with the model on the host env with --use-fast true and capture logs. If error trace shows "ValueError: tokenizer.json required for fast tokenizer" that's it.
priya: Got the trace earlier: "fast tokenizer: tokenizer.json not found -> using slow; warning: missing 'bos_token' metadata'" and our chat templates look for  only '<|system|>' marker. After fallback those markers map to plain tokens and generation prepended unexpected whitespace.
omar: Two options: 1) regenerate tokenizer.json using tokenizers library from vocab+merges (preferable), 2) update converter to always emit tokenizer.json (safer), 3) add a redwood runtime fallback that reconstructs specials from tokenizer_config.json.
sophia: For immediate unblock, you can copy tokenizer.json from huggingface repo if model repo has it. But that risks divergence if vocab/merges don't match exact version.
kevin: I'll sketch a small conversion patch: if tokenizer.json missing but vocab+merges present, run:
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.models import BPE
from tokenizers.trainers import BpeTrainer
# very small script: load vocab/merges -> build Tokenizer -> save tokenizer.json
```
priya: Nice. Can we push a quick fix to redwood-hf-converter to emit a minimal tokenizer.json and add a unit test?
omar: +1. Also add an eval check: after conversion run a tiny chat-template alignment test to ensure special tokens map. Failing that, mark model onboarding as "manual" until fixed.
kevin: I'll open a PR. assignment: kevin will add conversion emitter + test, priya will patch onboarding checklist to verify tokenizer.json presence and run the chat template smoke eval, sophia will run the quantization eval again once we have regenerated tokenizer.json.
priya: Deploy-bot, can you note that we blocked a dedicated bring-up until tokenizer.json is present?
deploy-bot: noted: ticket RID-1042 created, label=blocker, assignee=kevin, priority=high. CI job redwood/hf-converter/quick-smoke queued.
priya: Thanks — this explains the weird BLEU/regression numbers we saw on the 8-bit runs. I'll re-run the quantization sweep after the fix and post results here.
sophia: If anyone else sees a model with tokenizer_config.json only, tag #model-onboarding — we should add an automation that rejects bundles missing tokenizer.json in our internal registry.
kevin: Will do. PR incoming in ~2h.
priya: Great, closing loop. :thumbsup:
